suggestions.title: Log sodium today and Friday — it's the only field that can tell us if yesterday's half-pound was water

rationale.science: Sodium, carbohydrate and creatine move body water, not fat, and a day's swing can be worth a pound or more on the scale with nothing changed underneath (DASH-Sodium / Juraschek 2020; Powers 2003). That's why a salty day gets down-weighted rather than believed — but only if it's labelled as one.
rationale.data: Your sodium column is blank on 8/9, 8/10 and 8/12. The last entry is 8/11 'med'. Meanwhile your own measured water coefficient is +1.11 lb next-day after a high-sodium or alcohol day, and it priced two reads to the ounce: 8/9 predicted 164.48 against an actual 164.5, and again on 8/10.
rationale.relationship: You ate ~2,277 on 19,000 steps yesterday and the scale still went 164.2 to 164.7. With sodium logged that read either classifies as water and gets set aside, or it doesn't and becomes a real question. Blank, it stays ambiguous — and an ambiguous stall is exactly what your app's RATE FLOOR rule reads before it asks for a calorie trim. One field, three seconds, and it decides how the whole week gets interpreted.

suggestions.predict: If yesterday came in high-sodium, the trend gives back 0.5-1.1 lb within two mornings and reads at or under 163.6 by Saturday, and this week's stall closes as water. If it came in low or none and the scale is still at or above 164.5 on Saturday, the stall is real and I'll stop calling it noise.

suggestions.title: Press today: four honest sets or three — don't repeat Sunday's 8,8,7,4

rationale.science: On a cut you defend load rather than chase volume, and a working set is one taken near 1-3 reps in reserve. A fourth set that stops less than halfway to the other three isn't extra stimulus — it's an extra slot on the scorecard that the session then fails (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024; Grgic 2021).
rationale.data: 8/6: press 250 x 8,8,7 drew PRESS - TARGET MET. 8/9: the identical top three plus a fourth set at 4 reps drew no press row at all, while rows, tricep, sulek and lateral each got one from that same session. Press still reads 4 sets on file and today is your upper day — the first session since Monday.
rationale.relationship: Chest went 3 to 4 sets on 8/7, so the target list re-keyed to four slots and the app's target check needs every slot met. A 4-rep fourth set fails the whole conjunction and the lift scores nothing, however good the top three were. The target list isn't saved with the session, so this mechanism is my best guess rather than a proven fact — but the observable isn't a guess: the best press in your record scored zero and the set count was the only thing that changed.

suggestions.predict: Run four sets with an honest fourth, or run three, and press draws a feed row tonight. Repeat 8,8,7,4 and it draws nothing again and 250 stays ungraded a second session running. Withdrawal clause, restated: if you log four sets with a short fourth and press DOES produce a row, my reading is wrong and I'll retire it.

suggestions.title: The A/B your app started Tuesday still isn't on file — check for an arm before you train, and don't re-tap it

rationale.science: An A/B is worth its cost only because the assignment is recorded; that's the whole difference between it and just watching. Your own app says this about its Friday-vs-Tuesday comparison — without a controlled assignment it is 'a hint worth having, not a finding.' An unrecorded trial charges you the protocol and pays you no evidence.
rationale.data: The feed still carries TRIAL STARTED - THE FAILURE A/B - TRICEP CAPPED vs SULEK ALL-OUT dated 8/11. The trials list in your synced state is still empty, two days and one sync later.
rationale.relationship: A started trial is stored as { custom, started } with no id and no date. The sync merge keys trials on id or d and its union helper drops any record whose key comes back empty. So the trial dies at the first sync while the dated feed row survives — which is exactly the pair you're looking at. The decline path writes the same shape, so passing on it wouldn't stick either, and the guard that stops the proposal re-offering reads that same empty list.

suggestions.predict: Today's upper day prescribes no arm for tricep or sulek, and the same failure A/B can reappear in your inbox asking for consent again — re-tapping writes the identical unkeyable record. If today's protocol does name an arm for either lift, I've read this wrong and I'll withdraw it.
